vowelContrast.stress: Listen for stress. /ʌ/ is the main vowel in cup. /ə/ is the short, weak first vowel in about. Their vowel quality can be close, especially in American English.
vowelContrast.accent: Compare the same word, bird. The British /ɜ/ is a sustained vowel. American /ɝ/ adds the tongue shape for R throughout the vowel.
vowelContrast.rhoticStress: Both vowels have the American R sound. In bird, /ɝ/ is stressed. In teacher, /ɚ/ is short and unstressed at the end.

pronunciation.oneBeat: Say it in one beat and copy the tone from the sample.
pronunciation.approximationPause: Follow the arrows and pause briefly at |.
pronunciation.approximationTone: Follow the arrows. The Vietnamese accents suggest pitch direction.
pronunciation.apical: Keep your tongue near the position for the initial and sustain the sound. Listen to the sample.
pronunciation.fallback: Listen to the sample and say it in one beat.
pronunciation.pause: Pause briefly at the punctuation before continuing.
pronunciation.twoThirds: With two third tones together, the first usually rises like a second tone. Follow the sample for longer groups.
pronunciation.fallRise: Drop your pitch on the first syllable and raise it on the next. Keep the two beats together.
pronunciation.fallRiseN: Drop your pitch and finish with n, then move into the rising syllable in the same breath.
pronunciation.neutralNext: Make the next syllable short and light.
pronunciation.linkN: Finish the first syllable with n, then go straight into the next one.
pronunciation.linkSyllables: Keep the end of the first syllable and move straight into the next one in the same breath.
pronunciation.attachSounds: Connect the sounds in order. Keep any final consonant short and avoid adding a vowel after it.
pronunciation.linkWordsBody: Keep /{{end}}/ at the end of the first word and go straight into /{{start}}/.
pronunciation.listenAndCopy: Listen to and copy the reference sound.

englishSounds.k: Raise the back of your tongue to the soft palate and release the air.
englishSounds.ɡ: Use the same tongue position as /k/ and add voicing.
englishSounds.m: Close both lips and let the voiced sound out through your nose.
englishSounds.s: Bring your tongue close to the ridge behind your upper teeth and let air hiss through.
englishSounds.ʒ: Shape your tongue and lips as for /ʃ/, and add voicing.
englishSounds.h: Exhale gently with an open throat into the following vowel.
englishSounds.tʃ: Close with the front of your tongue just behind the upper gum ridge, then release into /ʃ/.
englishSounds.l: Touch your tongue tip to the ridge behind the upper teeth and let air pass around its sides.
englishSounds.j: Raise the front of your tongue as for /i/, then glide quickly into the vowel.
englishSounds.w: Round your lips and glide quickly into the next vowel.
englishSounds.ɛ: Keep your tongue forward and open your jaw a little more than for /ɪ/.
englishSounds.ɑ: Open your jaw and keep your tongue low and toward the back.
englishSounds.ɒ: Keep your tongue low and back with slightly rounded lips.
englishSounds.ɔ: Round your lips and raise your tongue slightly from the position for /ɒ/.
englishSounds.ʊ: Round your lips gently and keep the vowel short and relaxed.
englishSounds.u: Round your lips and keep your tongue high.
englishSounds.ʌ: Relax your lips, open your jaw slightly and keep your tongue near the center.
englishSounds.ɜ: Keep the tongue near the center with relaxed lips and hold the vowel.
englishSounds.ɝ: Keep the vowel stressed and draw your tongue into the English R position.
englishSounds.ɚ: Keep the vowel light while holding the English R tongue position.
englishSounds.eɪ: Glide from /e/ toward /ɪ/ in one syllable.
englishSounds.aɪ: Start with an open mouth and glide toward /ɪ/.
englishSounds.ɔɪ: Start with rounded lips and glide from /ɔ/ toward /ɪ/.
englishSounds.oʊ: Start with rounded lips and glide from /o/ toward /ʊ/.
englishSounds.əʊ: Start with relaxed lips, then round them as you glide toward /ʊ/.
englishSounds.aʊ: Open wide for /a/, then round your lips as you glide toward /ʊ/.
englishSounds.ɪə: Glide from /ɪ/ into a relaxed /ə/ within one syllable.
englishSounds.eə: Glide from a front vowel /e/ into a relaxed /ə/.
englishSounds.ʊə: Glide from a short rounded /ʊ/ to a relaxed /ə/.
englishSounds.p: Close both lips, then release a clear puff of air at the start of a stressed syllable. Keep your voice off until the vowel.
englishSounds.b: Close both lips and release with voicing.
englishSounds.t: Touch your tongue tip to the ridge behind your upper teeth and release.
englishSounds.d: Touch the ridge behind the upper teeth with your tongue and release with voicing.
englishSounds.n: Touch the ridge behind your upper teeth and let air out through your nose.
englishSounds.ŋ: Raise the back of your tongue and let air out through your nose.
englishSounds.θ: Put your tongue tip lightly between your teeth and let air pass.
englishSounds.ð: Put your tongue tip lightly between your teeth and add voicing.
englishSounds.f: Touch your lower lip to your upper teeth and let air pass.
englishSounds.v: Touch your lower lip to your upper teeth and add voicing.
englishSounds.ɹ: Hold the tongue tip away from the roof of the mouth. Avoid tapping or rolling it.
englishSounds.ɪ: Raise the front of your tongue slightly and keep it relaxed.
englishSounds.i: Raise the front of your tongue and spread your lips slightly.
englishSounds.æ: Open your mouth wide with the tongue forward.
englishSounds.ə: Relax your mouth and keep the vowel short and unstressed.
englishSounds.ʃ: Point the tongue towards the ridge behind the teeth and round the lips slightly.
englishSounds.z: Hold your tongue near the ridge behind your teeth and let out air with voicing.

initials.b: Close both lips and release with little air.
initials.p: Close both lips and release with a strong puff of air.
initials.m: Close both lips and let air exit through the nose.
initials.f: Lightly touch your lower lip to your upper teeth.
initials.d: Touch the ridge behind your upper teeth and release with little air.
initials.t: Touch the ridge behind your upper teeth and release with a strong puff of air.
initials.n: Touch the ridge behind your upper teeth and let air out through your nose.
initials.l: Touch the ridge behind your upper teeth and let air escape around the sides of your tongue.
initials.g: Raise the back of your tongue to the soft palate and release with little air.
initials.k: Raise the back of your tongue to the soft palate and release with a strong puff of air.
initials.h: Let air rub against the back of your mouth.
initials.j: Raise the front of your tongue towards the hard palate. Release through a narrow gap with little air.
initials.q: Use the same tongue position as j and release with a strong puff of air.
initials.x: Raise the front of your tongue towards the hard palate and let air flow continuously.
initials.zh: Raise and draw back the tongue tip, then release with little air.
initials.ch: Use the same tongue position as zh and release with a strong puff of air.
initials.sh: Raise and draw back the tongue tip and let air flow continuously.
initials.r: Raise the tongue tip as for sh and add voicing.
initials.z: Put the tongue tip near the ridge behind your upper teeth and release from a stop into friction with little air.
initials.c: Use the same tongue position as z and release with a strong puff of air.
initials.s: Bring the tongue tip close to the upper teeth and let air flow continuously.
initials.y: This spelling marks the start of a vowel. Start with i, or with rounded ü in yu.
initials.w: This spelling marks the start of a vowel. Start with rounded u and glide to the next vowel.

finals.a: Open your mouth wide and keep your tongue low.
finals.e: Keep your lips relaxed and draw your tongue back.
finals.ê: Open your mouth slightly and keep your tongue towards the front.
finals.i: Keep your tongue high and forward and spread your lips slightly.
finals.u: Round your lips and keep the tongue high and back.
finals.ü: Keep your tongue in the i position while rounding your lips as for u.
finals.ai: Glide from a to i in one beat.
finals.ei: Glide from e to i in one beat.
finals.ao: Glide from an open a to a rounded u in one beat.
finals.ou: Glide from o to u in one beat.
finals.an: Finish with n at the ridge behind the upper teeth.
finals.en: Start with a relaxed vowel and finish with n.
finals.ang: Open on a and finish with ng at the back of the mouth.
finals.eng: Start with a relaxed vowel and finish with ng.
finals.ong: Round your lips and finish with ng.
finals.er: Raise the tongue tip slightly as you make the vowel.
finals.ia: Glide from i to a in one beat.
finals.ie: Glide from i to e in one beat.
finals.iao: Glide from i through a to u in one beat.
finals.ian: Glide from i to an open e and finish with n.
finals.iang: Glide from i to a and finish with ng.
finals.in: Hold i and finish with n.
finals.ing: Hold i and finish with ng.
finals.iong: Glide from i to a rounded vowel and finish with ng.
finals.iu: Short for iou. Glide from i through o to u.
finals.uai: Glide from u through a to i.
finals.uan: Glide from u to a and finish with n.
finals.uang: Glide from u to a and finish with ng.
finals.ui: Short for uei. Glide from u through e to i.
finals.un: Short for uen. Start from rounded u and finish with n.
finals.ueng: Glide from u through a relaxed vowel to ng.
finals.üe: Start with rounded ü and glide to e.
finals.üan: Start with rounded ü, glide to an open e and finish with n.
finals.ün: Hold rounded ü and finish with n.

tones.0: No tone was entered, so the sample uses a neutral tone. Add a tone mark or a number from 1 to 5.
tones.1: Tone 1. Keep your pitch high and level.
tones.2: Tone 2. Raise your pitch from the middle to high.
tones.3: Tone 3. Drop low. It can rise again in isolation and often stays low within a phrase.
tones.4: Tone 4. Start high and drop your pitch quickly.
tones.5: Neutral tone. Say it briefly and lightly, following the previous syllable.

jSteps.0: Rest the tip of your tongue against the back of the lower teeth.
jSteps.1: Raise the front of your tongue towards the hard palate to block the airflow briefly.
jSteps.2: Lower the front of your tongue just enough to let air through a narrow gap, then move into i. Release with little air.

privacyPage.intro: Engclaw has no accounts and no telemetry or analytics. Your recordings, history and settings stay on this computer.
privacyPage.localBody: Speech recognition, pronunciation scoring and text-to-speech run locally. Your audio is never uploaded.
privacyPage.leavesHint: Only these connections are ever made, and only for the reason given.
privacyPage.hfBody: Downloads speech models when you choose to install them. No personal data is sent.
privacyPage.youtubeBody: Loads the video you open for shadowing, and its captions. YouTube may apply its own tracking inside its player.
privacyPage.githubBody: Checks for new releases and downloads updates. Turn this off under General > Check for updates.
privacyPage.wikimediaBody: Fetches word illustrations in the dictionary. Turn this off under General > Dictionary illustrations.
privacyPage.llmBody: Conversation messages go to the AI provider you configure. If you enable Shadowing translation, the displayed subtitle text is sent to that same provider for translation.
privacyPage.deleteBody: You can erase everything Engclaw stores under Your data at any time.
